statement: For a dimension-one principal open orbit, the subgroup of endpoints of actual finite-word paths starting at identity and fixing the entire principal base throughout acts trivially on every nonmetabelian nonopen frontier orbit. Hence two such original finite-word paths with identical complete principal-base paths have identical frontier restrictions there. For the full principal-base kernel, its intrinsic image on every such frontier orbit is central and closed discrete cyclic. The actual graph image in the product of the principal and frontier homeomorphism groups covers its quotient by this discrete kernel; that quotient maps by a continuous bijective homomorphism to the actual principal-base image, without an assertion of inverse continuity. Separately, inclusion of any connected component of an open planar domain intersected with an open Euclidean disk into the original domain is injective on fundamental groups. Null evaluation loops shrinking to a fixed frontier therefore admit fillings inside the original orbit with vanishing ambient diameter.
depends_on: C28 intrinsic one-dimensional orbit topology and compact finite-word tracks; C30 exact evaluation topology; C32 ambient-null restriction; C33 actual principal product and proper Lie action; C37/C48 one-dimensional translation and rotation comparisons; C38 actual closed discrete cyclic centralizers; the explicit planar regular-neighborhood and punctured-plane retraction argument
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison, nonfixed-frontier path comparison and controlled planar fillings
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Both homomorphisms are the actual principal-base action and intrinsic frontier restriction. Commutators are first proved identity on the open orbit and then on its closure. Intrinsic continuity is established for the specified compact finite-word paths, without assuming it for arbitrary unbounded word limits. The filling proof retains the original open domain and supplies an explicit strong deformation retraction of a punctured plane onto the relevant filled regular neighborhood. The full-kernel comparison retains both actual induced image topologies. Its kernel is closed and discrete in the graph image; the evenly covered neighborhoods are constructed directly. The final comparison is only a continuous bijective homomorphism.
notes: The finite-word principal-kernel endpoint set is a normal subgroup, and its intrinsic frontier image is path connected and abelian. Any nontrivial such image has no common fixed point by transitivity of the full image, so its one-dimensional orbits are open and it is transitive. Its free abelian transitive closure is the actual translation or rotation group; the full frontier image normalizes it and is therefore metabelian. This proves triviality under the stated nonmetabelian hypothesis and the exact path comparison. For the full principal kernel, commutator paths with arbitrary finite-word paths lie in the proved endpoint subgroup and therefore make the frontier image central. C38 makes this image closed discrete cyclic. In the actual product graph image, an identity neighborhood disjoint from its nontrivial discrete-kernel differences gives explicit evenly covered neighborhoods. Finite-word paths prove the graph image is path connected, so its full deck group is exactly that kernel. The induced map from the quotient to the principal-base image is a continuous bijection; inverse continuity is not asserted. For controlled fillings, a polygonal regular neighborhood is enlarged by filling only those inner disks lying entirely in the original domain. One excluded point is retained in every other inner disk, and explicit radial homotopies in the Jordan disk and exterior coordinates retract the punctured plane onto the enlarged neighborhood. This proves the small-disk fundamental-group injection and the existence of individual shrinking fillings. Neither part constructs an arbitrary moving-base lift, a frontier factorization for arbitrary source germs, a continuous family of fillings, or an equivariant fragmentation; C12 remains open.
